title: Dedicated pool billing reconciliation for burst usage and SLA adjustments
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Summary:
We need a robust reconciliation pipeline that produces auditable, per-customer billing events for Dedicated (reserved) capacity pools. The pipeline must correctly account for: 1) reserved throughput billed at committed rates, 2) burst consumption billed as overage at configured burst rates, 3) prorated reservation changes mid-billing-cycle, and 4) SLA credits for sustained missed latency or availability SLOs.

Problem background:
Customers purchase Dedicated pools that guarantee a committed throughput (tokens/sec or concurrent RPS). Existing billing relies on near-realtime counters that sometimes drift when: autoscaler resizes pools, requests are routed to compatible fallbacks, or service restarts clear in-memory counters. This causes disputes and manual credits. We also lack a clear method for retroactive adjustments when an SLA breach is determined after the fact.

Goals:
- Produce a deterministic per-customer invoice feed (line items) that reconciles reserved vs burst usage per billing window with traceable input events.
- Ensure reconciliation tolerates infra events (resizes/restarts) and supports retroactive SLA crediting without double-counting.
- Provide dashboards and alerts for anomalies and a runnable simulation harness for edge-case testing.

Non-goals:
- Changes to public pricing model. The ticket focuses on correctness and auditability of metering and credits, not pricing changes.
acceptance_criteria: Each billing window (UTC calendar month) produces a reconciliation report per customer with line items: reserved_units_charged, burst_units_charged, sla_credit_applied.
Reports are reproducible from raw event logs and produce the same numbers when re-run against the same input events.
Adjustments for pool resize events are deterministic and documented (prorate by time-in-state).
SLA credits are applied via a discrete adjustment line item that references the SLO runbook incident ID and the computed credit amount.
End-to-end integration tests cover: server restarts, autoscale up/down, cross-region failover, and retroactive SLA credit application.
New billing reports are surfaced in the finance dashboard and include itemized links to the underlying request traces and kernel-level counters.
tasks: Design reconciliation model (metrics, state snapshots, and post-processing rules)
Instrument runtime to emit immutable events: request_start, request_end, tokens_emitted, route_fallback, pool_resize, pool_assign
Create time-series snapshot service to record pool assignment and capacity at 1-minute resolution
Implement reconciliation job: ingest events + snapshots -> aggregate per-customer per-window
Handle prorating logic and define tie-breakers for mid-second changes
Implement SLA credit calculator and audit trail linking to incident IDs
Expose reconciliation output to billing pipeline and finance SFTP feed
Create dashboards (Anomaly, Drift, Reconciliation health) and alerting rules
Add unit/integration tests and a simulation harness for deterministic smoke tests
Run dry-run on last 3 months; compare with current invoicing and produce variance report
design_notes: Primary metering primitive will be immutable event stream (append-only). Avoid in-memory counters as source of truth.
Store 1-minute snapshots of pool topology so reconciliation can attribute requests to pool config at time of request.
Billing unit will be normalized token units (not raw bytes) to align with API pricing; conversion table in config.
When pool capacity changes mid-window, prorate reserved charge by wall-clock time weighted by committed_units at each minute snapshot.
Burst overage calculation: any validated usage above the prorated-reserved allocation within a minute is counted as burst. Bursts must be de-duplicated if request was retried.
SLA measurement window and credit policy follow SRE runbook: credit = min(monthly_reserved_charge, penalty_factor * downtime_seconds / window_seconds).
Retroactive SLA credits: create a 'billing_adjustments' stream that can be consumed by finance; adjustments reference original reconciliation job run_id and incident_id.

To avoid double-charging during fallback routing (customer routed from reserved pool to shared fallback), mark events with 'route_fallback' flag and attribute cost to fallback bucket instead of reserved bucket. Reserved billing should not count tokens consumed on fallback when fallback is billed separately.
implementation_notes: Events will be emitted from runtime with idempotency tokens so reconciliation can dedupe retries.
Use existing event bus (Kafka) with a dedicated topic 'metering.events' with schema versioning. Backfill compatibility must be handled (consumer ignores unknown fields).
Reconciliation job implemented as batch Spark/Beam job reading events + snapshots and writing line items to billing DB (billing.v1_line_items).
Store reconciliation artifacts (input offsets, job signature, checksums) for reproducibility and audit.
Add an intermediate 'candidate_invoice' table for finance to review before finalization; include variance_reason column.
Provide a lightweight API to trigger a recompute for a customer/month and to query the last-run signature.
schema_changes: Add billing.v1_line_items table (columns: customer_id, window_start, window_end, line_type, units, unit_price, amount_cents, source_job_id, source_offsets)
Add billing.billing_adjustments table (columns: adjustment_id, customer_id, reason, amount_cents, incident_id, created_at, applied_by)
Add runtime.event_metadata fields: idempotency_key, route_fallback, assigned_pool_id
Add snapshots.pool_capacity table with 1-minute resolution (pool_id, minute_ts, committed_units, available_units)
All schema changes must include backward-compatible migration path and clear purge policy (7 years retention by finance)
testing_plan: Unit tests for prorating function with boundary conditions (edge seconds, daylight-safe timestamps)
Integration test harness: simulated event stream replay covering upsizes/downsizing/fallbacks and verifying expected invoice line items
Chaos test: restart runtime components during heavy traffic and assert reconciliation remains deterministic when replayed
Dry-run reconciliation against past three months and produce variance dashboard; require <= 0.1% variance for high-volume customers
Manual review by finance on first two production runs before enabling automated finalization
observability: Reconciliation job exposes metrics: processed_events, late_events, deduped_events, job_runtime_seconds, checksum_mismatch_count
Create anomaly alert when post-run variance vs last-finalized > 1% for any customer with monthly spend > $5k
Dashboard: per-customer monthly breakdown of reserved_units, burst_units, sla_credits, and suspicious spikes
Trace links in line items to raw request traces and kernel counters for dispute resolution
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (engineering dry-run): run reconciliation for non-billable sandbox customers and validate outputs
Phase 2 (finance review): generate candidate invoices for 25 pilot customers and collect feedback
Phase 3 (limited billing): enable automated candidate->final for pilot cohort while keeping manual approval for the rest
Phase 4 (full): enable across all Dedicated customers after 2 successful months and finance sign-off
Rollback: keep existing invoices unchanged. If errors found, create reversal adjustments via billing_adjustments table and notify finance team
